How Edward Jones's disclosures and initiatives for younger investors compare to those of competitors cannot be assessed on a like-for-like basis on this evidence. Edward Jones discloses qualitative initiatives only — a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors, a minority stake in Quicken, and strategic aspirations — and reports no growth figures for younger clients (no growth figure for Edward Jones was found in the documents searched). Schwab, by contrast, discloses detailed quantitative metrics on younger clients (for example, approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households being Gen Z and millennials as of 2026-09-30) and names specific products (Schwab Starter Kit, Schwab Teen Investor Account, no/low commissions). Merrill's disclosed figure concerns its own under-40 advisors rather than younger clients, and Morgan Stanley and Raymond James Financial disclose nothing on the subject in the documents searched. The firms therefore measure and disclose different things, so their disclosures are not directly comparable.
